summary:
ARES (Astronaut Route Exploration & Safety System) is an intelligent Mars exploration and mission-planning system developed by Team StarPhi for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Focused on Gale Crater and Aeolis Palus, ARES brings together planetary science, geographic visualisation, geological information and astronaut route planning within an interactive exploration environment.
By connecting scientific observations from robotic Mars missions with future human exploration objectives, ARES helps users examine scientifically significant locations, understand regional terrain and visualise potential exploration routes. Its central vision is to transform complex planetary information into meaningful, accessible insights for Mars mission planning.
ARES bridges the knowledge gained through robotic exploration with the next frontier of human exploration, supporting a more informed approach to understanding and navigating the Martian surface.
details:
ARES — Astronaut Route Exploration & Safety System

1. Vision and Purpose

ARES is a Mars exploration and mission-planning system developed by Team StarPhi to connect planetary science, terrain intelligence and astronaut route planning.

Our vision is to make Mars exploration more informed by transforming scientific observations and planetary datasets into an interactive environment where exploration locations, geological significance and potential travel routes can be understood together.

ARES focuses on Gale Crater and Aeolis Palus, a region of Mars with a remarkable geological record preserved through ancient sediments, channels and evidence of past water activity.

2. The Challenge We Address

Planning human exploration of Mars requires more than identifying a destination. Mission planners must understand the surrounding terrain, evaluate geographical constraints, identify scientifically valuable locations and interpret information collected by previous robotic missions.

However, planetary observations and terrain information are distributed across different scientific resources. ARES brings these elements into a unified exploration environment to make their relationships easier to examine.

3. How ARES Works

ARES combines an interactive Martian map with geographic coordinates, scientific waypoints, geological information and proposed astronaut exploration routes.

The mission scenario begins at a hypothetical landing location on Aeolis Palus, near the historical Curiosity exploration region. From this starting reference, the system presents locations of scientific interest:

  • Rocknest: A windblown soil deposit investigated by Curiosity, where soil samples released water from hydrated components during heating.
  • Yellowknife Bay: An ancient sedimentary environment where analysis of Sheepbed mudstone revealed clay minerals and evidence of past aqueous conditions.
  • Peace Vallis: An ancient fluvial channel and alluvial-fan system that records the movement and deposition of water-transported sediments.

These locations connect the scientific legacy of robotic exploration with the objectives of a hypothetical future human mission.

4. Technology and Development

ARES is developed as an interactive web-based application using modern web technologies.

Its development involves:

  • React for the frontend application.
  • Leaflet for interactive geographic visualisation.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the web interface.
  • Planetary science resources, including Mars Global Surveyor MOLA topographic data, for regional terrain context.
  • Geographic coordinates and map-based route visualisation for mission planning.

The system is designed around modular map layers, scientific location information and mission-oriented visualisation.

5. Innovation and Creativity

The central innovation of ARES is the connection it creates between robotic planetary science and future human exploration.

Instead of presenting geological observations, terrain information and mission routes as separate elements, ARES brings them into a connected exploration environment.

Its approach allows users to understand the scientific importance of destinations alongside their geographical relationship to a proposed mission route. This creates a more meaningful way to explore planetary information and communicate mission-planning decisions.

6. Intended Impact

ARES aims to contribute to the future of planetary exploration by making complex Mars science information more accessible and useful for mission planning.

Its approach has potential applications in:

  • Human Mars exploration planning.
  • Scientific waypoint identification.
  • Planetary terrain visualisation.
  • Exploration route assessment.
  • Educational and research-based planetary mapping.

By connecting past discoveries with future exploration objectives, ARES presents a pathway towards more informed and science-driven exploration of the Martian surface.

7. Future Development

Future development will focus on expanding high-resolution terrain integration, improving elevation and slope analysis, strengthening route assessment, incorporating additional planetary datasets and advancing intelligent route-planning capabilities.

ARES represents StarPhi's commitment to developing technology that connects scientific understanding with the next generation of space exploration.
